cards.design_implication: When studying pulsar systems, high-precision timing arrays or equivalent instrumentation may be required to resolve relativistic effects like spin precession.
cards.evidence_excerpt: a precise measurement of relativistic spin precession in the double pulsar system
limitations: The text does not specify the instrument, method, or numerical value of the measurement.
This claim is restricted to the double pulsar system and may not generalize to other pulsar systems.
cards.statement: Relativistic spin precession was measured with precision in the double pulsar system.

cards.design_implication: Searches for millisecond pulsars should consider wide eccentricity ranges, including high eccentricities (e > 0.4), rather than assuming circular orbits.
does_not_establish: The formation mechanism of this system
The population fraction of such high-eccentricity systems
Whether this applies to globular cluster pulsars or other environments
cards.evidence_excerpt: a Galactic millisecond pulsar in an eccentric ( e = 0.44) orbit around an unevolved companion
limitations: This applies specifically to millisecond pulsars in the Galactic field.
The text does not establish whether this is typical or rare among millisecond pulsars.
cards.statement: At least one Galactic millisecond pulsar exists in an eccentric orbit with e = 0.44 around an unevolved companion.
